title: Dedicated capacity: circuit-breaker mis-eval blocked autoscale during tenant burst (customer escalation)
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
A paying Dedicated tenant (AcmeCorp) experienced a sustained traffic spike on 2026-02-09 which should have triggered burst allocation and a predictive scale-up. Instead the dedicated autoscaler refused to open burst headroom because the new circuit-breaker logic evaluated a stale burst-credit ledger snapshot and concluded the tenant exceeded its safe burst budget. The result: a cascade of coldstarts, request queueing, and multiple 5xx errors for ~22 minutes. Acme support escalated; they reported production impact to several customer-facing endpoints and sent a P0 support request.

What happened (high level):
- Autoscaler pipeline ingests headroom, burst-credit ledger, and telemetry to determine safe burst allocations.
- A recent change introduced a short-circuit in the circuit-breaker that prefers the cached ledger timestamp when telemetry ingestion is delayed by more than 10s.
- During the spike, a transient ingestion delay (~35s) due to a Kafka consumer GC pause left the cache with a pre-spike ledger snapshot. The circuit-breaker treated that stale snapshot as authoritative and prevented burst allocation.
- Fallback routing rules were insufficiently aggressive for this tenant (VIP), so requests remained queued rather than spilling to compatible hosted variants.

Immediate customer-visible symptoms:
- Increased 5xxs and latency for ~22 minutes (see Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/service/dedicated/AcmeCorp-2026-02-09)
steps_taken: 2026-02-09 09:18 UTC: Pager alert to oncall (latency+5xx) -> triage
2026-02-09 09:20 UTC: Scoped to dedicated autoscaler path after reserved-pool telemetry showed headroom drain
2026-02-09 09:28 UTC: Emergency config: disabled new circuit-breaker short-circuit on leader (rollout revert) -> immediate re-evaluation allowed burst open and traffic recovered
2026-02-09 10:05 UTC: Notified customer (AcmeCorp) with incident summary and mitigation steps
2026-02-10: Post-incident timeline and request for postmortem created in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood/incident/DED-2026-02-09-Acme-escalation
root_cause_summary: A combination of (1) a circuit-breaker optimization that trusted a cached burst-credit snapshot when telemetry lag >10s, and (2) an unrelated Kafka consumer GC pause that delayed ingestion long enough to produce a stale snapshot. The circuit-breaker lacked a conservative fail-open path for stale telemetry; instead it failed-closed, blocking burst allocations for the tenant.
fix_summary: Hotfix (rolled back) reverted the short-circuit behavior and added a temporary safety net: if telemetry lag >15s and current headroom < threshold, autoscaler will apply a conservative burst allowance (10% of requested burst) while emitting an elevated alert. Permanent fix in progress: improved ledger reconciliation (idempotent merge), heartbeat-based telemetry freshness metric, and expanded canary coverage for circuit-breaker changes.
